title: Dahal government bans TikTok (November 2023)
description: The government of Prime Minister Pushpa Kamal Dahal banned TikTok in November 2023, saying it disrupted social harmony, goodwill and spread indecent material. The ban was lifted in August and September 2024.

title: Ministry notice: social media platforms must list within three months under the 2080 directive
description: Notice posted on the ministry site on 15 Mangsir 2080 (1 Dec 2023) on the Directive for Regulating the Use of Social Media 2080, approved by the cabinet on 2080/7/23 and published in the Nepal Gazette on 2080/08/11. Social media platforms operating at the time of the directive must list with the ministry within three months of the notice and those without an office in Nepal must set up an office or contact point within three months; the ministry may stop operation in Nepal of platforms that do not list. The directive in Nepali and English is said to be on the ministry website.
document_url: {"url": "https://giwmscdnone.gov.np/media/app/public/22/posts/1701416487_66.pdf", "label": "Notice on regulating the use of social media, Ministry of Communication and Information Technology (Nepali, 1 December 2023)"}

title: Home ministry posts the 2081 procedure for assessing damage from public protests
description: Procedure titled "Procedure for assessing damage caused by public demonstrations, strikes and protest programmes, 2081", posted on the MoHA website on 2081-01-18 (1 May 2024). Its provisions could not be read as text.
document_url: {"url": "https://moha.gov.np/upload/e66443e81e8cc9c4fa5c099a1fb1bb87/files/%E0%A4%B8%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%9C%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%95_%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A6%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B6%E0%A4%A8_%E0%A4%B9%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B2_%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%BE_%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A7%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%BE_%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%AC%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%9F_%E0%A4%B9%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%87_%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B7%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%BF_%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%82%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%99%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A8.pdf", "label": "Procedure for assessing damage caused by public demonstrations, strikes and protest programmes, 2081 (Nepali)"}

title: CPJ: arrest of Kantipur Media Group chair appears aimed at muzzling its reporting
description: CPJ reported the arrest of Kailash Sirohiya, chair of Kantipur Media Group, over alleged citizenship irregularities, and said it "appears to be an effort to muzzle the critical reporting of Nepal's largest media group".
document_url: {"url": "https://cpj.org/2024/05/chair-of-nepals-largest-media-group-arrested-after-publication-of-reports-alleging-fraud/", "label": "Source page"}

title: President Paudel appoints Oli prime minister
description: President Ram Chandra Paudel appointed CPN-UML chairman KP Sharma Oli prime minister on the strength of Nepali Congress backing.
document_url: {"url": "https://www.newsonair.gov.in/k-p-sharma-oli-appointed-nepals-new-prime-minister", "label": "K P Sharma Oli appointed Nepal's new Prime Minister"}

title: Oli cabinet of 22 sworn in
description: President Paudel administered the oath of office and secrecy to 19 newly appointed ministers; with the prime minister and two deputy prime ministers the cabinet had 22 members. Portfolios include Home (Ramesh Lekhak, Congress), Foreign Affairs (Arzu Rana, Congress), Finance (Deputy PM Bishnu Prasad Paudel, UML), Defence (Manbir Rai) and Communications (Prithvi Subba Gurung, UML).
document_url: {"url": "https://kathmandupost.com/national/2024/07/15/prime-minister-oli-forms-22-member-cabinet", "label": "Prime Minister Oli forms 22-member cabinet"}

title: Oli reads out the seven-point Nepali Congress-CPN-UML agreement
description: Oli disclosed the seven-point agreement: a national consensus government, Oli leading for two years from formation, then Nepali Congress president Sher Bahadur Deuba leading until the general elections in December 2027, with commitments on constitutional amendment, the economy and corruption.
document_url: {"url": "https://en.himalpress.com/oli-discloses-contents-of-seven-point-pact-reached-between-nc-uml/", "label": "Oli discloses contents of seven-point pact reached between NC, UML"}

title: Cabinet lifts the TikTok ban
description: At a regular Thursday meeting the cabinet decided to lift the ban on TikTok after Prime Minister Oli directed that all social networking sites be treated equally. The decision followed TikTok's assurances to the government.
document_url: {"url": "https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2024/8/23/nepal-lifts-tiktok-ban-after-blocking-app-over-social-harmony-concerns", "label": "Nepal lifts TikTok ban after blocking app over 'social harmony' concerns"}

title: NTA directs internet providers to lift the TikTok block
description: The Nepal Telecommunications Authority directed all internet and mobile service providers to remove the restriction on TikTok.
document_url: {"url": "https://www.timesofoman.com/article/149563-nepal-formally-ends-ban-on-tiktok-isps-ordered-to-lift-embargo", "label": "Nepal formally ends ban on TikTok, ISPs ordered to lift embargo"}

title: Parliamentary special committee report on cooperative fraud names Lamichhane
description: A parliamentary special inquiry committee concluded that Rabi Lamichhane was involved in misusing cooperative funds that were funnelled into Gorkha Media Network.
document_url: {"url": "https://myrepublica.nagariknetwork.com/news/cooperative-fraud-case-rabi-lamichhane-found-complicit-dhanraj-gurung-to-be-investigated/", "label": "Cooperative fraud case: Rabi Lamichhane found complicit, Dhanraj Gurung to be investigated"}

title: Supreme Court verdict: online and social media platforms must register
description: Extended full bench verdict in the contempt case against sidhakura.com stating that domestic or foreign online and social media platforms should be mandatorily registered with the competent authority before operation. Date disputed between sources.
document_url: {"url": "https://kathmandupost.com/national/2025/08/17/top-court-says-all-social-media-online-sites-must-register", "label": "Top court says all social media, online sites must register"}

title: CIB arrests Rabi Lamichhane
description: A Central Investigation Bureau team arrested Rabi Lamichhane at his party's central office to investigate cooperative fraud and organised crime.
document_url: {"url": "https://kathmandupost.com/national/2024/10/19/lamichhane-arrested-on-fraud-organised-crime-charges", "label": "Lamichhane arrested on fraud, organised crime charges"}

title: Social Media Bill tabled in the National Assembly
description: The Bill on the Operation, Use and Regulation of Social Media was tabled in the National Assembly by Communications Minister Prithvi Subba Gurung. It provides fines up to NPR 2.5 million for operating without registration, prison terms up to five years for users, and bars anonymous accounts. Date disputed (27 Jan, 29 Jan, 9 Feb).
document_url: {"url": "https://nepaleconomicforum.org/key-highlights-and-implications-of-the-social-media-bill-2081-bs-2025-ad/", "label": "Key highlights and implications of the Social Media Bill 2081 BS (2025 AD)"}

title: Ministry notice: platforms to list with the ministry and name a contact point in Nepal (3 Feb 2025)
description: Notice posted on the ministry site on 21 Magh 2081 (3 Feb 2025). It tells persons, companies and organisations that operate or wish to operate social media platforms to list with the ministry and to provide a point of contact in Nepal as required by clauses 3 and 6 of the Directive for Regulating the Use of Social Media 2080, and states that the ministry can stop operation in Nepal of a platform that does not comply.
document_url: {"url": "https://giwmscdnone.gov.np/media/pdf_upload/np_lbvhbni.pdf", "label": "Notice on regulating the use of social media, Ministry of Communication and Information Technology (Nepali, 3 February 2025)"}

title: CPJ urges lawmakers to reject the social media bill
description: CPJ listed provisions it objected to (prohibitions on "false or misleading information" and "gruesome content", a ban on anonymous profiles, prison terms up to five years, platform licence revocations) and said lawmakers should refuse the bill unless it is significantly revised.
document_url: {"url": "https://cpj.org/2025/02/cpj-nepal-lawmakers-should-reject-social-media-bill-threatening-press-freedom/", "label": "Source page"}

title: Joint statement urges revising the Media Council and social media bill
description: CPJ joined more than two dozen media and civil society groups calling on Nepal to revise the social media bill and the new Media Council, citing "overbroad and vague provisions" and the speed with which both were introduced.
document_url: {"url": "https://cpj.org/2025/03/cpj-joins-call-for-nepal-to-revise-new-media-council-social-media-bill/", "label": "Source page"}

title: Ministry warns platforms to register within one month
description: Onlinekhabar reports the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology warned on 20 March 2025 that platforms would be blocked if they did not register within one month.

title: Cabinet removes Kulman Ghising from the Nepal Electricity Authority
description: The Cabinet decided to remove Nepal Electricity Authority executive director Kulman Ghising and appoint Shakya (as printed) in his place, after a standoff over dues owed by industrialists and an unauthorised energy trade deal with India.
document_url: {"url": "https://kathmandupost.com/national/2025/03/24/government-sacks-kulman-ghising-as-nea-chief", "label": "After long standoff, government sacks Kulman Ghising"}

title: Nepal Army deployed in Koteshwor after the curfew
description: The Nepal Army was deployed on the streets of Koteshwor to restore order after the curfew began.
document_url: {"url": "https://thehimalayantimes.com/kathmandu/pro-monarchy-protesters-attack-media-offices-set-fire-to-annapurna-post-office", "label": "Pro-monarchy protesters attack media offices, set fire to Annapurna Post office"}

title: Curfew order for Tinkune, Baneshwar and Koteshwor
description: The district administration imposed a curfew from 4:25 pm in Tinkune, Koteshwor and Sinamangal; the Kathmandu Post gives 4:25 pm to 10 pm on Friday, extended until 7 am Saturday.
document_url: {"url": "https://kathmandupost.com/national/2025/03/29/protest-leaders-incite-violence-which-turns-deadly", "label": "Protest leaders incite violence which turns deadly"}

title: Minister Gurung vows accountability for the Tinkune violence
description: Communications Minister and government spokesperson Prithvi Subba Gurung said the guilty would be held accountable, and condemned attacks on media houses; the report mentions a probe committee.
document_url: {"url": "https://newsonair.gov.in/nepal-government-spokesperson-minister-gurung-vows-legal-action-against-guilty-of-fridays-violent-protests", "label": "Nepal government spokesperson minister Gurung vows legal action against guilty of Friday's violent protests"}

title: Police arrest Durga Prasai
description: Nepal Police arrested Durga Prasai and an associate in Bhadrapur, Jhapa, on charges of crimes against the state and organised crime linked to the 28 March violence.
document_url: {"url": "https://www.newsonair.gov.in/nepal-police-arrest-medical-entrepreneur-political-activist-durga-prasai/", "label": "Nepal police arrest medical entrepreneur, political activist Durga Prasai"}

title: Kathmandu District Court remands Durga Prasai for 12 days
description: The Kathmandu District Court remanded Durga Prasai and an associate to judicial custody for 12 days for further investigation.
document_url: {"url": "https://thehimalayantimes.com/kathmandu/durga-prasai-sent-to-judicial-custody-for-12-days", "label": "Durga Prasai sent to judicial custody for 12 days"}

title: Bidya Bhattarai resigns as education minister
description: Education Minister Bidya Bhattarai resigned amid differences with the prime minister and finance minister; a health reason was also stated.
document_url: {"url": "https://kathmandupost.com/national/2025/04/22/education-minister-resigns-after-rift-with-pm-finance-minister", "label": "Education minister resigns after rift with PM, finance minister"}

title: Supreme Court upholds Lamichhane's custody
description: The Supreme Court upheld Rabi Lamichhane's custody in the cooperative fraud case, saying it could not reasonably be believed on the available evidence that the defendants were innocent.
document_url: {"url": "https://kathmandupost.com/national/2025/05/23/supreme-court-upholds-custody-of-rabi-lamichhane-in-cooperative-fraud-case", "label": "Supreme Court upholds custody of Rabi Lamichhane in cooperative fraud case"}

title: RSF urges parliament to keep news media out of the Social Media Bill
description: RSF called on parliament to amend the Social Media Bill so that news media fall outside its scope, and said impunity for crimes against journalists keeps putting the profession at risk.
document_url: {"url": "https://rsf.org/en/nepal-rsf-calls-action-amid-endangered-press-freedom", "label": "Source page"}

title: HRW calls on police to withdraw arrest warrant against journalist
description: HRW said police were trying to arrest a well-known journalist over claims on his YouTube channel about a leading political family's business interests, and that the arrest warrant should be withdrawn.
document_url: {"url": "https://www.hrw.org/news/2025/06/18/nepal-police-search-for-journalist-who-reported-on-political-familys-business", "label": "Source page"}

title: HRW submission to the Universal Periodic Review of Nepal
description: HRW's UPR submission said the Electronic Transactions Act "continues to be used to arrest and prosecute journalists and members of the public for legitimate online expression" and that Nepal had not implemented numerous recommendations it supported in the previous review.
document_url: {"url": "https://www.hrw.org/news/2025/07/11/submission-to-the-universal-periodic-review-of-nepal", "label": "Source page"}

title: Access Now calls on Nepal to reverse the Telegram ban
description: Access Now said the Nepal Telecommunications Authority had instructed providers to block Telegram on 18 July 2025 and called on authorities to "Immediately revoke the directive blocking access to Telegram, restore access, and refrain from imposing platform bans".
document_url: {"url": "https://www.accessnow.org/press-release/keepiton-nepal-authorities-must-reverse-nationwide-telegram-ban-and-uphold-human-rights/", "label": "Source page"}

title: Cabinet directs platforms to register within one week
description: A Cabinet decision, dated 25 August 2025 by Onlinekhabar and Swarajya and 26 August by Radio Nepal, directed that all social media platforms operating in Nepal register within one week. Minister Prithvi Subba Gurung later cited the decision and a Supreme Court directive.
document_url: {"url": "https://giwmscdnone.gov.np/media/pdf_upload/BHADRA%20CABINET%202082_uk0h2ym.pdf", "label": "Decisions of the Council of Ministers, Bhadra 2082 (Nepali; meetings of Bhadra 2, 9, 13, 23 and 30)"}

title: CPJ report: police and courts retaliate as journalists expose corruption
description: CPJ documented cases of retaliation against journalists in Nepal in 2025, including a contempt of court case opened by the Supreme Court against publisher Kanak Mani Dixit and an order by the Press Council to take down news items.
document_url: {"url": "https://cpj.org/2025/08/backlash-nepals-police-courts-retaliate-as-journalists-expose-corruption/", "label": "Source page"}

title: Communications ministry notice: social media platforms must register within seven days
description: The Ministry of Communication and Information Technology required unregistered social media platforms to register by 4 September 2025, in line with the Supreme Court directive, designating a point of contact, a resident grievance handling officer and a compliance officer.
document_url: {"url": "https://radionepalonline.com/en/2025/08/28/415736.html", "label": "Radio Nepal Online report on the social media registration notice"}

title: CPJ calls for the social media ban to be rescinded
description: CPJ said Nepal's ban "sets a dangerous precedent for press freedom" and that "The government must immediately rescind this order and restore access to social media platforms".
document_url: {"url": "https://cpj.org/2025/09/nepal-orders-ban-on-major-social-media-platforms/", "label": "Source page"}

title: Ministry directs NTA to block unregistered platforms
description: After a meeting of the ministry, the NTA, telecom operators and internet service providers chaired by Minister Prithvi Subba Gurung, the ministry directed the NTA to block access to platforms that had not registered. Reported figures range from about two dozen to 27 platforms; 26 is the most common. Registered platforms stayed available. The block was later withdrawn (BBC says on Monday night 8 September).

title: NTA instructs internet service providers to block platforms
description: The NTA instructed mobile and internet service providers to block the listed platforms and, per Swarajya, told the Internet Service Providers Association of Nepal to enforce it through a technical committee. Swarajya expected restrictions to begin from Friday evening.

title: NHRC urges the government to reconsider the decision to close social media
description: Press release of 20 Bhadra 2082 (5 Sep 2025), signed by the NHRC spokesperson, expresses serious concern about the government decision to close social media platforms, says it restricts freedom of expression and access to information under the Constitution and international covenants, and directs the government to reconsider and adopt alternative means of regulation and management.
document_url: {"url": "https://nhrcnepal.org/uploads/press_release/NHRC_Nepal_Press_Release_2082-5-20.pdf", "label": "NHRC press release: reconsider the decision to close social media (Nepali, 20 Bhadra 2082)"}

title: X asks ministry for registration documents
description: On Friday 5 September 2025 X emailed the ministry asking which documents it needed to register; the ministry replied by email, per spokesperson Gajendra Thakur. Swarajya separately reports the ministry confirmed Meta had emailed inquiries about documentation requirements.

title: Kathmandu District Security Committee meets, finds situation normal
description: The committee met on 7 September 2025 and concluded the overall security situation was normal, calling for stronger coordination. The Karki Commission found no written Central Security Committee decision on a protest strategy for 5 to 10 September.

title: National Investigation Department report on planned Gen Z protest
description: A six-point NID report dated 7 September 2025, obtained by Onlinekhabar, said activists and groups were preparing demonstrations against the ban in Kathmandu Valley and other districts, that a group had asked the district administration for security arrangements, and that Balen Shah had voiced support. It named possible participants. Its text says the march would start "from 8 a.m. on September 7", which is probably a slip for 8 September.

title: Oli speech: nation’s independence greater than jobs of a handful
description: In a speech on Sunday 7 September 2025, before the protest, Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli said he would not tolerate the nation being undermined and asked how it could be acceptable to defy the law and the constitution. Al Jazeera separately quotes him, undated, saying young people cannot think independently.

title: Permission for the Maitighar protest sought from the district administration
description: Sources disagree on who obtained or sought permission. Al Jazeera and India Today say the district administration or local media said Hami Nepal had secured approval. Onlinekhabar says two individuals went to the Kathmandu District Administration Office on 7 September. The NID report says a Gen Z group asked for security arrangements. The NHRC report (via HimalPress) says the rally began within boundaries permitted by the chief district officer.

title: Amnesty calls for an independent investigation into the deaths
description: Amnesty condemned "the unlawful use of lethal and less-lethal force by law enforcement" and said the government "must also immediately conduct a thorough, independent and impartial investigation into the deaths".
document_url: {"url": "https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2025/09/nepal-accountability-for-deadly-crackdown-on-gen-z-protesters/", "label": "Source page"}

title: Curfew in Butwal-Bhairahawa, 4 pm to 10 pm
description: Rupandehi District Administration Office imposed a curfew order in the Butwal-Bhairahawa area from 4 pm to 10 pm, under Section 6(A) of the Local Administration Act, 2028.

title: Cabinet withdraws the social media ban
description: After an emergency cabinet meeting the government withdrew the ban and the ministry ordered agencies to resume social media. Communication Minister Prithvi Subba Gurung was quoted by local media. AFP found all major apps working in Kathmandu on Tuesday.

title: Cabinet forms committee to investigate the violence
description: The Monday-evening cabinet meeting at Baluwatar decided to form an inquiry committee; All India Radio says terms of reference were to be submitted within 15 days. The Kathmandu Post (via ANN) says the government formed a probe committee.

title: Curfew extended to Singha Durbar, Parliament, presidential and vice-presidential offices
description: Curfew extended to the administrative core of Kathmandu, including Singha Durbar, the Parliament building, the offices of the President and Vice President and the Narayanhiti Museum area (Himal Press); ANI adds the prime minister's residence. INSEC lists Baneshwor, Singha Durbar, Baluwatar and Sheetal Niwas.

title: Curfews in Biratnagar, Birgunj and Kavrepalanchok
description: Himalayan Times reports curfews in Koshi Province's Biratnagar (11 am to 10 pm), Birgunj (11 am to 6 pm, extended) and Kavrepalanchok (from 12:15 pm), and in Kathmandu and Lalitpur areas.

title: Hospitals instructed to treat injured protesters free
description: All India Radio reports the Ministry of Health earlier instructed hospitals to provide free treatment to all injured protesters.

title: Home Minister Ramesh Lekhak resigns
description: Lekhak tendered his resignation to Prime Minister Oli during the Cabinet meeting at Baluwatar on Monday evening, on moral grounds, after Nepali Congress leaders called for it.

title: Curfew order around New Baneshwar, 12:30 pm to 10 pm
description: Kathmandu District Administration Office imposed a curfew from 12:30 pm to 10 pm covering Baneshwor Chowk to Bijuli Bazar bridge (west), Tinkune Chowk (east), Ratna Rajya School (north) and Shankhamul bridge (south). HRW notes the government ordered the curfew at around 12:30 pm; Kathmandu Post says few in the crowd heard the order.

title: Nepali Army deployed in New Baneshwor
description: Himalayan Times, at 1:25 pm, reports the Nepali Army was deployed in New Baneshwor as the situation intensified.

title: NHRC urges restraint, relief and free treatment
description: The National Human Rights Commission urged restraint and called on authorities to provide relief and compensation to victims' families and free treatment for the injured, according to ANI.
document_url: {"url": "https://thehimalayantimes.com/nepal/nhrc-urges-authorities-to-halt-excessive-force-against-gen-z-protesters", "label": "The Himalayan Times"}

title: OHCHR spokesperson calls for a prompt and transparent investigation
description: Ravina Shamdasani said OHCHR called on authorities "to respect and ensure the rights of peaceful assembly and freedom of expression", asked for "a prompt and transparent investigation" into the killings, and urged reconsideration of social media regulation.
document_url: {"url": "https://news.un.org/en/story/2025/09/1165796", "label": "Source page"}

title: Oli tells cabinet the protest was infiltrated
description: According to the Kathmandu Post (via ANN), during the Monday cabinet meeting Oli said the peaceful demonstration was infiltrated by disruptive elements while expressing sensitivity toward youth demands.

title: Indefinite prohibitory order in Pokhara from 2 pm
description: Kaski District Administration imposed an indefinite prohibitory order in the Pokhara area bounded by Shahid Chowk, Milan Chowk, Fistel Gate (Baidam), the Land Revenue Office and Rastrabank Chowk, from 2 pm until further notice. Kantipur separately reports an indefinite curfew order.

title: Access Now calls for independent investigation of deadly force and digital repression
description: Access Now said it was "deeply alarmed by the government of Nepal's violent crackdown on human rights, both online and off" and called for a full and independent investigation of the use of deadly force.
document_url: {"url": "https://www.accessnow.org/press-release/access-nows-statement-on-nepals-escalating-digital-repression-and-deadly-crackdown/", "label": "Source page"}

title: Army chief's appeal to protesters
description: Army chief Ashok Raj Sigdel asked protesters to suspend protest programmes and come for talks in a video message.

title: Army moves ministers and leaders to safe locations
description: The army airlifted ministers from Bhaisepati, and moved Oli, Dahal and Madhav Kumar Nepal to Shivapuri. Kantipur counts 61 people airlifted.

title: FIDH, OMCT and others call for accountability and a permanent rollback of the ban
description: FIDH, OMCT, FORUM-ASIA, CIVICUS and nine Nepali organisations urged authorities to "immediately end all forms of violence and repression against peaceful protestors", make the rollback of the ban permanent, and conduct a "prompt, impartial, and independent investigation into all killings and injuries".
document_url: {"url": "https://www.fidh.org/en/region/asia/nepal/nepal-call-for-accountability-over-protest-crackdown-urging-an-end-to", "label": "Source page"}

title: HRW: police fire on Gen Z protest, investigate and prosecute
description: HRW said police killed at least 19 people and injured over 300, called for prompt, impartial investigation and discipline or prosecution of those responsible, and urged UN Peacekeeping to bar implicated officers and units from future missions. Meenakshi Ganguly is quoted.
document_url: {"url": "https://www.hrw.org/news/2025/09/09/nepal-police-fire-on-gen-z-protest", "label": "Source page"}

title: India MEA: deeply saddened, urges restraint and dialogue; advisory to nationals
description: India's Ministry of External Affairs said it was "closely monitoring the developments in Nepal" and was deeply saddened by the loss of many young lives, hoped all concerned would exercise restraint and use peaceful means and dialogue, and advised Indian nationals in Nepal to exercise caution and follow Nepali authorities' guidelines.
document_url: {"url": "https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/world/closely-monitoring-situation-in-nepal-india-asks-its-nationals-to-exercise-caution", "label": "Source page"}

title: Joint statement by foreign missions urges maximum restraint
description: Foreign missions in Kathmandu said they were deeply saddened by the violence and loss of life, reaffirmed support for the rights to peaceful assembly and freedom of expression, and urged all parties to exercise maximum restraint. Reports differ on the signatories: seven (B360 Nepal) or nine (Diplomat Nepal).
document_url: {"url": "https://diplomatnepal.com/?p=19831", "label": "Source page"}

title: Kathmandu curfew order
description: Tribune reports the Kathmandu District Administration Office announced a curfew from 08:30 until further notice. Setopati and Al Jazeera confirm curfew orders existed and were defied.

title: Nepali Congress general secretaries ask Deuba to recall ministers
description: The general secretaries said the seven-point agreement with CPN-UML no longer applied, called on Oli to resign and urged Deuba to recall all ministers.

title: Nepal Army deployment in Kathmandu
description: Troops were stationed in Kathmandu and at the airport from the evening of 9 September, with deployment alongside other security forces from 10 pm local time.

title: Army deployment and 22:00 ultimatum
description: The army said it and all security agencies would control the situation from 22:00, and that looters should return weapons by then. Troops patrolled Kathmandu that night.

title: Oli's resignation letter
description: Oli wrote to President Paudel that he resigned as prime minister effective that day under Article 77(1)(a), 'to pave the way for a constitutional political course' (Himal Press) or to facilitate a constitutional political solution (Himalayan Times, Setopati).

title: Health Minister Pradip Paudel resigns
description: Paudel announced he was stepping down from the Ministry of Health and Population.

title: Water Supply Minister Pradip Yadav resigns
description: Yadav announced on Facebook that he was stepping down in support of the protests and against the crackdown.

title: President accepts Oli's resignation
description: President Ram Chandra Paudel accepted the resignation with immediate effect. Himalayan Times stamps the report at 15:03.

title: President's appeal for restraint and dialogue
description: The President appealed to all parties to be restrained and to come to the negotiating table, including Gen Z representatives.

title: President keeps the Council of Ministers in function under Article 77(3)
description: The President's Office said the current Council of Ministers would continue to run the government until a new one was formed, citing Article 77(3).

title: Agriculture Minister Ram Nath Adhikari resigns
description: Adhikari announced his resignation and emailed his letter to Oli on Tuesday.

title: RPP lawmakers resign
description: Thirteen federal and 28 provincial RPP lawmakers resigned on Tuesday afternoon, and the party said the government, Parliament and Constitution had lost relevance.

title: RSP lawmakers resign
description: RSP lawmakers announced their resignations one after another; Setopati later counted twenty and reported the party divided over dissolving the House.

title: Joint appeal of army, security agencies and top civil servants
description: The Nepali Army, other security agencies, the Chief Secretary and the Home Secretary jointly called for a peaceful solution through political dialogue and urged restraint.

title: Youth and Sports Minister Tejulal Chaudhary resigns
description: Kantipur reports Chaudhary resigned after the use of force against the protests.

title: UN rights chief Türk calls for a thorough, impartial investigation
description: Volker Türk said he was appalled by the escalating violence, cited "concerning reports of unnecessary and disproportionate use of force by the security forces", urged restraint and dialogue, and called for an urgent, thorough, transparent and impartial investigation.
document_url: {"url": "https://www.arabnews.com/node/2614694/", "label": "Source page"}

title: UN in Nepal statement: pained by loss of lives, calls for proportionate policing and prompt independent investigation
description: One-page statement dated 9 September 2025, Kathmandu. The UN in Nepal says it is deeply pained by the loss of lives and rising tensions, calls on protesters to exercise freedom of expression and assembly peacefully, urges authorities to keep law enforcement proportionate and in line with international human rights standards, and says all allegations of excessive use of force should be investigated promptly, independently, transparently and impartially.
document_url: {"url": "https://nepal.un.org/sites/default/files/2025-09/Statement%20by%20the%20United%20Nations%20in%20Nepal.pdf", "label": "Statement by the United Nations in Nepal, 9 September 2025"}

title: UN Secretary-General statement on Nepal
description: The Secretary-General's spokesperson said the Secretary-General was "deeply saddened by the loss of life". B360 Nepal and The Himalayan Times report that he urged a thorough investigation, restraint and dialogue; NewsGram reports the spokesperson saying authorities must "protect and respect the rights of peaceful assembly and freedom of expression".
document_url: {"url": "https://www.newsgram.com/asia/2025/09/09/nepal-govt-protesters-to-hold-discussions", "label": "Source page"}

title: China foreign ministry hopes Nepal restores order; no Chinese casualties reported
description: Spokesperson Lin Jian said China hoped sectors in Nepal would handle domestic issues properly and restore order, that there were no reports of casualties among Chinese citizens, and that Chinese nationals had been advised to take precautions.
document_url: {"url": "https://www.theweek.in/wire-updates/international/2025/09/10/fgn50-china-ld-nepal.html", "label": "Source page"}

title: CPJ: media outlets torched and journalists injured
description: CPJ reported that protesters set fire to the offices of Kantipur Media Group and Annapurna Post, that at least four journalists were injured, and said "Authorities should hold both security forces and demonstrators to account for all assaults on the media".
document_url: {"url": "https://cpj.org/2025/09/nepal-protests-media-outlets-torched-and-journalists-injured-in-deadly-unrest/", "label": "Source page"}

title: Nepali Congress general secretaries' self-critical statement
description: Congress general secretaries said they were self-critical that efforts to hold the government accountable were incomplete and urged a constitutional path.

title: Nepal Army arrests and loot recovery
description: The army reported 27 arrests between 10 pm on Tuesday and 10 am on Wednesday, NPR 3.37 million of looted cash recovered, and 31 firearms seized (23 in Kathmandu, 8 in Pokhara).

title: Nepali Congress general secretaries urge the President to stay on the constitutional track
description: Nepali Congress general secretaries Bishwa Prakash Sharma and Gagan Thapa said in a joint statement that the President must hold discussions with all parties and that no new political structure can be created outside due process.

title: NHRC continues monitoring after the 23-24 Bhadra events and appeals for calm
description: Press release of 25 Bhadra 2082 (10 Sep 2025) says the Commission continues monitoring the human rights situation and the condition of the families of the dead and the injured during the curfew, asks all parties to help rights defenders, journalists and essential service providers move freely, calls for non-violence, and urges a political way out through democratic processes.
document_url: {"url": "https://nhrcnepal.org/uploads/press_release/NHRC_Nepal_Press_Release-2082-5-25.pdf", "label": "NHRC press release: continued monitoring after the events of Bhadra 23 and 24 (Nepali, 25 Bhadra 2082)"}

title: Movement restriction until 17:00 then curfew until 06:00 Thursday
description: Setopati reports movement restrictions until 17:00 on 10 September, then a curfew until 06:00 on Thursday, with ambulances, hearses, fire trucks, health workers and security vehicles exempt.

title: CPN-UML statement on a constitutional solution
description: CPN-UML said the solution after the prime minister's resignation must be sought constitutionally, asked the President to start dialogue and condemned the arson and vandalism.

title: Army eases curfew schedule (11 September)
description: Prohibitory order 10 am to 5 pm and curfew 7 pm of 11 September to 6 am of 12 September; air travellers allowed to move on showing tickets.

title: Dahal: Gen Z demands can be met within the Constitution
description: Pushpa Kamal Dahal said the demands could be fulfilled within the Constitution and the current parliamentary process.

title: CPN (Maoist Centre) statement on the Gen Z protests
description: The Maoist Centre blamed the Congress-UML coalition and the crackdown, said infiltrators were behind arson and vandalism, and warned against unconstitutional exits.

title: President Paudel statement seeking a solution within the constitution
description: Paudel said he was consulting and making every effort to find a way out within the constitutional framework, and urged restraint.

title: Supreme Court press release on arson at courts; habeas corpus hearings to resume from 29 Bhadra
description: Press release of 26 Bhadra 2082 (11 Sep 2025), signed by Chief Justice Prakash Man Singh Raut, expresses sorrow for the deaths and wishes the injured a quick recovery, regrets the arson, vandalism and looting at courts on 24 Bhadra that destroyed documents, equipment and vehicles, and states that the Supreme Court will begin registering and regularly hearing habeas corpus petitions from 29 Bhadra, as decided by an emergency full-court meeting.
document_url: {"url": "https://supremecourt.gov.np/web/assets/downloads/onwards24/5-26pressbigyapti.pdf", "label": "Supreme Court press release: condolences, arson at courts, habeas corpus hearings to resume (Nepali, 26 Bhadra 2082)"}

title: Appointment of Sushila Karki as interim prime minister
description: President Ram Chandra Paudel appointed former Chief Justice Sushila Karki interim prime minister. The appointment was announced by the President's spokesman Kiran Pokhrel on 12 September 2025, ahead of the evening oath.

title: Army notice denying takeover and monarchy reports
description: The Nepal Army issued a notice asking people not to believe false comments linking the army to a takeover or restoration of the monarchy.

title: Army revises curfew hours (12 September)
description: Movement allowed 6-11 am and 5-7 pm in Kathmandu, Bhaktapur and Lalitpur; prohibitory order 11 am to 5 pm; curfew 7 pm to 6 am. Gatherings, demonstrations and protests stayed prohibited.

title: British Embassy welcomes Karki
description: The British Embassy in Kathmandu called Karki's appointment an important step and affirmed support for accountability and inclusive governance.

title: Dissolution of the House of Representatives
description: Notification of the President's Office dissolving the House of Representatives with effect from 11 pm on 12 September 2025, on the recommendation of the Karki government (first cabinet meeting at 11 pm per ANI). Challenged as unconstitutional by the major parties and, from October, in the Supreme Court.

title: Election date set for 5 March 2026
description: President Paudel announced in a statement late on 12 September that fresh elections would be held on 5 March 2026 and urged all stakeholders to use the "hard earned opportunity" to hold the election on time.

title: India MEA welcomes interim government
description: India welcomed the formation of the interim government led by Karki and said it hoped for peace and stability.

title: Amnesty, ICJ, FIDH and HRW: commit to rule of law and independent investigation
description: Four organisations called on all stakeholders to publicly commit to the rule of law and human rights obligations, for the army chief to instruct soldiers to respect human rights, and for a "prompt, thorough, independent, credible, time-bound, transparent and effective investigation" into police use of force, plus accountability for corruption.
document_url: {"url": "https://www.hrw.org/news/2025/09/12/nepal-protesters-demand-integrity-rights-rule-of-law", "label": "Source page"}

title: NHRC tells the President a solution should rest on human rights, democratic values and the rule of law
description: Press release dated Bhadra 27, 2082 (12 Sep 2025) says the Commission is in communication with President Ram Chandra Poudel, has conveyed that a solution grounded in human rights, democratic values and the rule of law would be appropriate, and is in contact with other stakeholders. Published in Nepali and English.
document_url: {"url": "https://nhrcnepal.org/uploads/press_release/NHRC_Press_Release_2082-5-27_eng.pdf", "label": "NHRC press release: a solution should be sought on human rights, democratic values and the rule of law (English, 12 September 2025)"}

title: RSF: more than a dozen media outlets targeted, journalists injured
description: RSF said more than a dozen media outlets and three journalists' organisations were attacked on 9 September and that police violence injured four journalists, calling the attacks "unacceptable".
document_url: {"url": "https://rsf.org/en/political-crisis-nepal-more-dozen-media-outlets-targeted-journalists-injured", "label": "Source page"}

title: Supreme Court meets the bar by video on reviving case files destroyed by arson
description: Press release of 27 Bhadra 2082 (12 Sep 2025) says a Zoom meeting was held between the Chief Justice, the justices, the Nepal Bar Association, the Supreme Court Bar Association, senior advocates, the Chief Registrar and registrars on the damage of 24 Bhadra, covering revival of destroyed case files, running benches, security of justices, lawyers and staff, and rebuilding IT services; the Chief Justice also instructed court staff in a separate discussion.
document_url: {"url": "https://supremecourt.gov.np/web/assets/downloads/onwards24/5-27prssbijapti.pdf", "label": "Supreme Court press release: Zoom meeting with the bar on reviving destroyed case files (Nepali, 27 Bhadra 2082)"}

title: UN in Nepal statement on Karki appointment
description: UN Resident Coordinator Hanaa Singer-Hamdy said the UN stands with the people of Nepal in their aspirations for peace, justice, transparency, accountability and progress.

title: UN Resident Coordinator: UN stands alongside the people of Nepal
description: The UN Resident Coordinator said the UN stands alongside the people of Nepal in their aspirations for peace, justice, transparency, accountability and progress, on the day Sushila Karki was appointed interim prime minister.
document_url: {"url": "https://news.un.org/en/story/2025/09/1165839", "label": "Source page"}

title: US Embassy shelter-in-place advisory to US citizens
description: Business Today reported that the US Embassy in Kathmandu issued a shelter-in-place advisory to American citizens, urging them to avoid non-essential travel; Nepal also offered stranded tourists visa regularisation without extra cost.
document_url: {"url": "https://www.businesstoday.in/amp/nri/visa/story/stranded-tourists-in-nepal-get-free-visa-extensions-amid-protests-us-warns-citizens-to-shelter-493771-2025-09-12", "label": "Source page"}

title: Curfew and restrictive orders lifted (13 September)
description: A Nepal Army spokesperson said there were no restrictive orders or curfew on Saturday 13 September.

title: EU ambassador welcomes Karki
description: EU Ambassador Veronique Lorenzo welcomed the appointment of the first woman PM and said the EU looks forward to supporting the interim administration.

title: Modi message to Karki
description: PM Narendra Modi posted on X wishing Karki well and saying India remains committed to the peace, progress and prosperity of Nepal's people.

title: Nepali Congress calls dissolution unconstitutional
description: The Nepali Congress said the move to dissolve parliament is against the spirit of the constitution and the Supreme Court's interpretation, and "absolutely unconstitutional". CPN-UML and CPN (Maoist Centre) also condemned it.

title: NHRC urges escaped prisoners to return to jail and those holding seized weapons to return them
description: Press release of 28 Bhadra 2082 (13 Sep 2025) appeals to prisoners who left jails during the Bhadra 23 and 24 protests to return, and to those who took weapons from security forces to return them. It says the Commission received information that the escapes caused fear and insecurity in society and that inmates of juvenile reform homes also left.
document_url: {"url": "https://nhrcnepal.org/uploads/press_release/NHRC_Nepal_Press_Release-2082-5-28.pdf", "label": "NHRC press release: prisoners to return to jail and return seized weapons (Nepali, 28 Bhadra 2082)"}

title: China congratulates Karki
description: A Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson congratulated Karki on becoming prime minister of the interim government and spoke of a time-honoured friendship.

title: Eight parties demand reversal of dissolution
description: Eight parties (Nepali Congress, CPN-UML, CPN Maoist Centre, CPN Unified Socialist, Janata Samajbadi Party, Loktantrik Samajbadi Party, Nagarik Unmukti Party, Janamat Party) called the dissolution unconstitutional and demanded that it be reversed.

title: Japan welcomes Karki's appointment
description: The Embassy of Japan said it welcomed Karki's appointment as an important step in the transition and hoped for a swift and peaceful democratic transition.

title: Karki announces martyr status and compensation
description: On taking charge, Karki said those killed on 8 September would be called martyrs and their families given one million Nepali rupees each; the government would bear the injured's expenses.

title: Karki's first address: six-month pledge
description: In her first public remarks as prime minister Karki said "We will not stay here more than six months in any situation" and that her name had been "brought from the streets".

title: President Paudel: "The constitution has been saved"
description: In a signed statement on 14 September the President said a peaceful release had been achieved, that the constitution and parliamentary democracy had been saved, and asked all sides to help hold the 5 March elections.

title: Rights groups joint statement after Karki's appointment
description: International rights groups issued a joint statement demanding an end to "impunity of the past"; Amnesty International's Isabelle Lassee said Nepal is at a turning point.

title: US Embassy welcomes interim government
description: The US Embassy welcomed the restoration of calm and said it looks forward to working with the interim government as Nepal prepares for new elections; it commended the President, youth leaders and the Nepali Army.

title: Cabinet decisions: martyr status, mourning day and relief
description: Setopati reports the cabinet declared those killed on 8 and 9 September martyrs, set 17 September as a day of mourning, agreed a high-level inquiry committee (structure to be finalised) and Rs 1.5 million per deceased family.
document_url: {"url": "https://giwmscdnone.gov.np/media/pdf_upload/BHADRA%20CABINET%202082_uk0h2ym.pdf", "label": "Decisions of the Council of Ministers, Bhadra 2082 (Nepali; meetings of Bhadra 2, 9, 13, 23 and 30)"}

title: NHRC calls for post-mortems, funerals, relief and a return to lawful protest
description: NHRC urged authorities to "ensure post-mortem examinations, dignified funerals, and relief for families of those killed during the recent Gen Z protests", and asked that demands be presented through democratic and lawful processes.
document_url: {"url": "https://thehimalayantimes.com/nepal/nhrc-urges-calm-accountability-and-protection-of-rights", "label": "Source page"}

title: Oath of the first three ministers
description: President Paudel administered the oath of office and secrecy to Rameshwor Khanal, Kulman Ghising and Om Prakash Aryal.

title: NHRC officials meet Chief of the Army Staff Ashok Raj Sigdel
description: Press release of 31 Bhadra 2082 (16 Sep 2025) says NHRC officials met Chief of the Army Staff Ashok Raj Sigdel at the Commission and discussed peace and security and the condition of those under the protection of the Nepali Army, and that the Commission advised the Army to act within democracy, human rights and the rule of law. It also states that the Commission is in continuing contact with Gen-Z representatives, families of the dead, the injured and others affected.
document_url: {"url": "https://nhrcnepal.org/uploads/press_release/NHRC_Nepal_Press_Release-2082-5-31.pdf", "label": "NHRC press release: meeting between NHRC officials and the Chief of Army Staff (Nepali, 31 Bhadra 2082)"}

title: Cabinet forms a committee to assess loss and damage from the 23-24 Bhadra protests
description: Item 3 of the cabinet meeting of Asoj 5, 2082 forms a five-member committee, convened by the secretary of the National Planning Commission, to assess loss and damage to public property, physical infrastructure and private institutions in the Bhadra 23 and 24 protests and to prepare a reconstruction plan. Item 2 of the same meeting allows public bodies to make urgent special-circumstance procurement to restore offices and services.
document_url: {"url": "https://giwmscdnone.gov.np/media/pdf_upload/CABINET%202082%20ASOJ_7uide2h.pdf", "label": "Decisions of the Council of Ministers, Asoj 2082 (Nepali; meetings of Asoj 5, 9, 12, 23 and 30)"}

title: Judicial inquiry commission formed
description: Cabinet constituted a three-member judicial inquiry commission led by Gauri Bahadur Karki to investigate police atrocities and arson and vandalism on 8 and 9 September; three months to report.

title: Government forms inquiry commission under Gauri Bahadur Karki
description: Three-member high-level commission formed on 21 September 2025 under Gauri Bahadur Karki with a three-month mandate to identify causes of the violence, vandalism, looting and arson and recommend action. Members: Bigyan Raj Sharma and Bishweshwor Prasad Bhandari. It reported on 8 March 2026, about five and a half months after formation; the retrieved sources do not say whether the deadline was extended.
document_url: {"url": "https://giwmscdnone.gov.np/media/pdf_upload/CABINET%202082%20ASOJ_7uide2h.pdf", "label": "Decisions of the Council of Ministers, Asoj 2082 (Nepali; meetings of Asoj 5, 9, 12, 23 and 30)"}

title: Recommendation of five new ministers
description: Karki recommended Anil Kumar Sinha, Mahabir Pun, Madan Prasad Pariyar, Jagdish Kharel and Sangeeta Mishra; ANI reports four sworn in on 22 September.

title: Dahal proposes dissolving all Maoist Centre committees
description: Pushpa Kamal Dahal proposed dissolving all existing committees of the Maoist Centre and electing all office bearers directly at the general convention. The Kathmandu Post calls it the first party restructuring after the uprising.

title: NHRC appeals to stakeholders to protect civil rights and restore normal life after the Gen-Z protests
description: Press release of 6 Asoj 2082 (22 Sep 2025) says damage to public and private property and state structures in the Gen-Z movement poses a serious challenge to the rule of law and rights. It calls for urgent reconstruction and repair of offices of security bodies, courts, prisons, juvenile reform homes and district administration offices, and for fair and quick assessment of damage and compensation.
document_url: {"url": "https://nhrcnepal.org/uploads/press_release/NHRC_Nepal_Press_Release-2082-6-6.pdf", "label": "NHRC press release: appeal for civil rights and normal life (Nepali, 6 Asoj 2082)"}

title: Cabinet decides financial assistance for families of the identified dead
description: Item 12 of the cabinet meeting of Asoj 9, 2082 provides each family of an identified Nepali citizen who died in the Bhadra 23 and 24 protests with Rs 10 lakh in financial assistance plus Rs 5 lakh for funeral, food and transport costs. Prisoners and juvenile-home inmates who died while escaping during the unrest are excluded in the text.
document_url: {"url": "https://giwmscdnone.gov.np/media/pdf_upload/CABINET%202082%20ASOJ_7uide2h.pdf", "label": "Decisions of the Council of Ministers, Asoj 2082 (Nepali; meetings of Asoj 5, 9, 12, 23 and 30)"}

title: Cabinet decides identification, treatment and relief measures for the injured
description: Item 7 of the cabinet meeting of Asoj 12, 2082 directs the home ministry to issue identity documents to the injured in the Bhadra 23 and 24 protests, the health ministry to designate hospitals for follow-up care with Gen-Z clinics and free travel, to set up a hotline, to form a technical committee to classify the injured, and to give an interim Rs 20,000 per injured person through the district administration offices.
document_url: {"url": "https://giwmscdnone.gov.np/media/pdf_upload/CABINET%202082%20ASOJ_7uide2h.pdf", "label": "Decisions of the Council of Ministers, Asoj 2082 (Nepali; meetings of Asoj 5, 9, 12, 23 and 30)"}

title: Passports of Oli and four officials frozen
description: The government froze the passports of Oli, Ramesh Lekhak, former home secretary Gokarna Mani Duwadi, former National Investigation Department chief Hutaraj Thapa and former Kathmandu chief district officer Chhabi Rijal in connection with the suppression of the 8-9 September protests.

title: Original Facebook post of the 'Malacañang slingshot' clip reported taken down
description: VERA Files reported on 2 October 2025 that the original viral Facebook post of a Nepal Parliament protest video presented as a slingshot attack on Malacañang Palace, with more than 10 million views, had been taken down, while similar posts remained on other platforms. VERA Files does not say who removed it.

title: Cyabra publishes analysis of fake accounts in Gen Z protest discourse
description: Cyabra said 34 percent of sampled profiles on X in protest-related discourse were fake, that they generated 11.5 percent of engagements and had a potential reach of 326 million views. Reported by Republica and Onlinekhabar on 7 October 2025.

title: Supreme Court resumes writ registrations from a tent
description: The Supreme Court resumed registering writ petitions on Tuesday 14 October 2025, the first time since the 9 September arson; the building had burned and the court was working from a tent. More than seven petitions against House dissolution arrived on the first day (the Kathmandu Post reports 14 petitions on 15 October, ten on dissolution).

title: Petitions at Supreme Court challenge Karki government and House dissolution
description: The Supreme Court received 14 writ petitions on 15 October 2025; ten related to House dissolution and government formation and sought to reinstate Parliament and revoke Karki's appointment. No ruling was reported in the retrieved article.

title: Cabinet declares 45 of the dead martyrs
description: A cabinet meeting on Monday 3 November 2025 declared 45 people who died in the movement martyrs, based on a Home Ministry committee study with security agencies and district administration offices. The Kathmandu Post gives 76 deaths in total.
document_url: {"url": "https://giwmscdnone.gov.np/media/pdf_upload/CABINET%202082%20KARTIK_kvl6cyv.pdf", "label": "Decisions of the Council of Ministers, Kartik 2082 (Nepali; meetings of Kartik 12, 17 and 24)"}

title: Cabinet appoints Dan Bahadur Karki as police chief
description: A cabinet meeting on Monday 10 November 2025 appointed senior-most additional inspector general Dan Bahadur Karki, then chief of the Kathmandu Valley Police Office, as Inspector General. Chandra Kuber Khapung was replaced on retiring after 30 years of service on the following Wednesday.
document_url: {"url": "https://giwmscdnone.gov.np/media/pdf_upload/CABINET%202082%20KARTIK_kvl6cyv.pdf", "label": "Decisions of the Council of Ministers, Kartik 2082 (Nepali; meetings of Kartik 12, 17 and 24)"}

title: Home ministry site publishes the procedure for classifying people injured in the Gen-Z protest
description: Procedure titled "Procedure for classification of the injured in the Gen-Z protest, 2082", issued under the Public Health Service Act 2075, for assessing, classifying and documenting people injured in the Gen-Z protest and movement of 2082/5/23 and 24 by severity of injury so that treatment and relief can be prioritised. It refers to a technical committee formed by the Council of Ministers on 2082/6/12 (28 Sep 2025). Date shown is the posting date on the MoHA website.
document_url: {"url": "https://moha.gov.np/upload/e66443e81e8cc9c4fa5c099a1fb1bb87/files/%E0%A4%9C%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%9C%E0%A5%80_%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A6%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B6%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%BE_%E0%A4%98%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%B9%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%82%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B_%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%A3_%E0%A4%B8%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AC%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%80_%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A7%E0%A4%BF_%E0%A5%A8%E0%A5%A6%E0%A5%AE%E0%A5%A8.pdf", "label": "Procedure for classification of the injured in the Gen-Z protest 2082 (Nepali)"}

title: HRW report: unlawful use of force during the Gen Z protest
description: HRW said security forces used disproportionate force on 8 September, "killing seventeen people in Kathmandu", analysed video showing Nepal Police and the Armed Police Force firing at protesters, and called on the Karki government to investigate excessive force as well as arson and mob attacks.
document_url: {"url": "https://www.hrw.org/news/2025/11/20/nepal-unlawful-use-of-force-during-gen-z-protest", "label": "Source page"}

title: Gen Z youth and Bara security committee reach six-point verbal deal
description: At talks at the Armed Police Force Technical School in Pathahiya, officials agreed to address all six demands raised by Gen Z youth after the Simara clash. The date is the article date.

title: Amnesty report: "We went there to raise our voice, not to be killed"
description: Amnesty's briefing and statement said at least 19 people were killed and more than 300 injured on 8 September, that kinetic impact projectiles were fired directly into dense crowds without warning, and recommended the government review its approach to assemblies and amend laws on the use of force. It also cites 76 dead and more than 2,000 injured nationwide.
document_url: {"url": "https://www.amnesty.org/en/documents/asa31/0529/2025/en/", "label": "Source page"}

title: Agreement to release those charged only for joining the protests
description: The Kathmandu Post of 5 October 2026 says a 10 December 2025 agreement stipulated that people under investigation or charged purely for taking part in the 8-9 September protests would be released. The parties to the agreement are not named in the retrieved text.

title: High court orders RSP chair Lamichhane's release on bail
description: The Butwal bench of the Tulsipur High Court ordered Rabi Lamichhane's release on bail on Thursday 18 December 2025 in the Supreme Cooperative fraud case; he left Nakkhu prison on Friday 19 December after depositing Rs 374.84 million.

title: FNJ report: 139 press freedom violations in 2025
description: The Federation of Nepali Journalists recorded 139 press freedom violations in 2025 against 60 the year before, and 26 incidents during the 8-9 September protests that affected more than 100 journalists and media institutions.
document_url: {"url": "https://fnjnepal.org/np/freedom/27", "label": "Source page"}

title: Kulman Ghising resigns as energy minister
description: Energy Minister Kulman Ghising resigned on 7 January 2026, reportedly after Prime Minister Karki asked ministers considering contesting the 5 March election to resign. He said he had not yet taken RSP membership.

title: Deuba-aligned committee suspends Gagan Thapa and Bishwa Prakash Sharma
description: The central working committee suspended general secretaries Gagan Thapa and Bishwa Prakash Sharma and joint general secretary Farmullah Mansur for five years for calling the special general convention without the establishment faction's consent. The special convention hall annulled the action, according to a search-result summary of another outlet.

title: Election Commission recognises Thapa-led Nepali Congress
description: The Election Commission recognised the Gagan Thapa-led Nepali Congress as the legitimate party, citing the statute's special-convention provision, delegates' supreme authority and no recorded dissent over the convening. The Deuba camp said it would fight the ruling.

title: Election code of conduct 2026 enforced
description: The Election Commission enforced the Election Code of Conduct, 2026 from 19 January for the 5 March House of Representatives election.

title: HRW: investigate the September violence and corruption allegations
description: HRW said police killed 19 protesters in the September demonstrations and called on the interim government to ensure that "the September violence, and also recent allegations of corruption, are thoroughly investigated".
document_url: {"url": "https://www.hrw.org/news/2026/02/04/nepal-protests-over-corruption-inequality-and-social-media-ban", "label": "Source page"}

title: HRW, Amnesty and ICJ urge publication of reports on the crackdown
description: The three organisations urged the interim government to publish all reports documenting violations against protesters and asked parties to commit to ending impunity. HRW says at least 76 people were killed.

title: HRW, Amnesty and ICJ call for publication of the Commission of Inquiry report
description: The three organisations called on Nepal to "release the Commission of Inquiry report into deadly violence during the 'Gen Z' protests of September 2025", said at least 76 people were killed, most unlawfully, and reported that the commission deadline was extended beyond the election day.
document_url: {"url": "https://www.hrw.org/news/2026/02/12/nepal-publish-reports-on-violent-crackdowns-on-protests", "label": "Source page"}

title: Cabinet receives the inquiry commission report on the 23-24 Bhadra protests
description: Item 29 of the cabinet meeting of Chaitra 1, 2082 records that the Council of Ministers accepts (receives) the report submitted by the inquiry commission formed to investigate the Bhadra 23 and 24 protests.
document_url: {"url": "https://giwmscdnone.gov.np/media/pdf_upload/CABINET%202082%20chaitra_veoiplv.pdf", "label": "Decisions of the Council of Ministers, Chaitra 2082 (Nepali; meetings of Chaitra 1, 13, 16, 22 and 24)"}

title: Karki commission recommends investigation of arson and looting
description: The commission led by Gauri Bahadur Karki recommended an in-depth investigation to identify those involved in widespread arson, looting and vandalism on 9 September 2025 (Bhadra 24), and criminal action against members of a group it calls TOB. The Kathmandu Post notes it largely stays silent on the second day of violence.

title: Prime Minister Karki decides to publish the commission report
description: Himal Press reports the prime minister decided on Wednesday evening to publish the report, after media outlets had published it. The Kathmandu Post reported the leaked content on 26 March. The Wednesday is taken to be 25 March from the article date.

title: Home ministry site publishes the procedure for relief assistance to people injured in the Gen-Z protest
description: Procedure titled "Procedure for providing relief assistance to persons injured in the Gen-Z protest and movement of Bhadra 23 and 24, 2082", issued by the Ministry of Home Affairs. The cover page carries the title and the ministry seal only; its provisions could not be read as text. Date shown is the posting date on the MoHA website (2082-12-12).
document_url: {"url": "https://moha.gov.np/upload/e66443e81e8cc9c4fa5c099a1fb1bb87/files/GenZ.pdf", "label": "Procedure for providing relief assistance to persons injured in the Gen-Z protest and movement of Bhadra 23 and 24, 2082 (Nepali)"}

title: Cabinet decides to implement the commission report
description: After Balendra Shah's swearing-in, a cabinet meeting decided to implement the report of the High-Level Inquiry Commission, recommending criminal investigation and prosecution of Oli, Lekhak and Khapung. IANS says the meeting was held 'on the same day' as the arrests (28 March), which conflicts with other summaries placing it after the swearing-in on 27 March.
document_url: {"url": "https://giwmscdnone.gov.np/media/pdf_upload/CABINET%202082%20chaitra_veoiplv.pdf", "label": "Decisions of the Council of Ministers, Chaitra 2082 (Nepali; meetings of Chaitra 1, 13, 16, 22 and 24)"}

title: Arrest of Oli and Lekhak on negligence charges
description: Nepal Police arrested Oli and Lekhak at their homes in Bhaktapur. Home Minister Sudan Gurung said it was not revenge. Oli said it was retaliatory.

title: Government announces 100-point governance roadmap
description: The roadmap includes a rehabilitation package for Gen Z protest victims (employment, skill development, psychosocial counselling) and the immediate start of investigations and legal action based on the Karki commission report.

title: Kathmandu District Court grants five-day remand
description: A single bench of judge Ananda Shrestha remanded Oli and Lekhak to five days in custody. Prosecutors had sought 10 days. Lekhak appeared in person; Oli, being treated at Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital, appeared virtually. Defence lawyers said there were no grounds for detention.

title: Supreme Court declines to release Oli and Lekhak
description: The Supreme Court declined on Monday 30 March to release the two after petitions alleging illegal detention, according to OCCRP.

title: Former Kathmandu chief district officer Chhabi Rijal arrested
description: A Kathmandu Valley Crime Investigation Office team arrested Chhabi Rijal at his Koteshwor home on Tuesday 31 March 2026, following the Karki commission's recommendations. The Himalayan Times dates the earlier arrests of Oli and Lekhak to 27 March, against 28 March elsewhere.

title: US lowers Nepal travel advisory to Level 2
description: The State Department lowered its Nepal advisory to Level 2, "Exercise Increased Caution", citing "an improved security situation following the end of nationwide demonstrations that began in September 2025". It noted that demonstrations "can start with little warning and may quickly turn violent".
document_url: {"url": "https://myrepublica.nagariknetwork.com/news/us-lowers-nepal-travel-advisory-to-level-2-urges-caution-over-potential-unr-92-73.html", "label": "Source page"}

title: House elects Dol Prasad Aryal Speaker
description: Dol Prasad Aryal of the RSP was declared elected unopposed as Speaker.

title: Supreme Court orders investigation concluded or suspects freed
description: On Monday 6 April the Supreme Court ruled that authorities must either formally conclude the investigation or free the suspects, citing health, equal treatment with others released in similar cases, and that the main investigative steps were done.

title: Oli and Lekhak released on condition of availability
description: Authorities released Oli and Lekhak on Thursday 9 April after about two weeks of detention, on the condition that they remain available to investigators. Kantipur notes this is release from custody, not from charges. The Kathmandu Post quotes Oli saying he was detained unlawfully for 13 days.

title: Cabinet forms committee to study security agencies' role
description: A cabinet meeting on Wednesday 15 April formed a committee under former High Court judge Prem Raj Karki, with former APF AIG Subodh Adhikari and former police AIG Tek Prasad Rai, to study the commission report and security mechanisms.

title: Supreme Court full court decides how courts handle case files lost in the 23-24 Bhadra events
description: Decision of the Supreme Court full court meeting of 2 Baisakh 2083 (15 Apr 2026) titled "deadlock arising from the events of Bhadra 23 and 24, 2082". The decision sets out how courts should proceed on case files that were destroyed or cannot be recovered, on missing criminal-fine and penalty records, and on seized property, with the first item referring to the 2082 directive on recovery and certification of destroyed case files. A covering letter dated 10 Baisakh 2083 (23 Apr 2026) from the registrar sends the certified decision to all courts.
document_url: {"url": "https://supremecourt.gov.np/court/public/media/2026_04/d57f1efa934ada7bdb31893bf2087bf8.pdf", "label": "Supreme Court full-court decision of 2 Baisakh 2083 on the deadlock arising from the events of Bhadra 23 and 24, 2082, with covering letter of 10 Baisakh 2083 (Nepali)"}

title: Sudan Gurung resigns as home minister
description: Gurung resigned over scrutiny of his financial dealings and alleged ties to a businessman under money-laundering investigation, to allow an impartial investigation. Prime Minister Shah took the Home portfolio in the interim.

title: Armed Police AIG Poudel promoted to Inspector General despite commission recommendation
description: AIG Narayan Dutta Poudel was promoted to Inspector General of the Armed Police Force as Raju Aryal retired. The Karki commission had recommended departmental action against Poudel; the government cited seniority.

title: HRW and partners urge Balen government to ensure accountability
description: The organisations called for those responsible for violations during the Gen Z protests to be brought to justice, a credible transitional justice process, and release of unpublished official reports on lethal violence against popular movements since 1990.

title: HRW, Amnesty and ICJ urge the new government to deliver accountability
description: The three organisations urged the new government to "bring those responsible for human rights violations during the Gen Z protest to justice" and to complete the transitional justice process in line with international standards.
document_url: {"url": "https://www.hrw.org/news/2026/04/30/nepal-balen-government-should-bring-human-rights-reforms", "label": "Source page"}

title: Government finalises list of 2,660 injured
description: The government finalised the verified injured list at 2,660. Of 250 names recently recommended, 22 were approved. Recognised injured are eligible for quotas in education, employment and medical treatment.

title: NHRC report recommends legal action and a five-year political ban for Oli and others
description: NHRC submitted a report to the government that, according to OCCRP, recommended "sweeping legal action and a five-year political ban" for former Prime Minister Oli, two former ministers and senior security officials, and blamed them for the violence on 8 and 9 September. Himal Press says it identified "the failure of state mechanisms and the excessive use of force by security agencies".
document_url: {"url": "https://www.occrp.org/en/news/nepal-rights-body-urges-charges-against-ex-pm-over-gen-z-protest-deaths", "label": "Source page"}

title: NHRC submits report recommending action against Oli and others
description: The National Human Rights Commission submitted its report to the government on Wednesday 27 May 2026. It held Oli primarily responsible (his refusal to lift the social media ban was called the direct trigger), also named Ramesh Lekhak and former communications minister Prithvi Subba Gurung, recommended action against named security officers, free lifetime medical treatment for the injured, and, per OCCRP, investigation of 17 RSP lawmakers including Rabi Lamichhane. Himal Press confirms findings of state failure and excessive force but not the named ministers.
document_url: {"url": "https://nhrcnepal.org/uploads/press_release/NHRC_Nepal_Press_Note-2083-2-13.pdf", "label": "NHRC press note: recommendations of the Gen-Z movement investigation report sent to the government (Nepali, 13 Jestha 2083)"}

title: Nepali Congress demands the government's position on the NHRC report
description: The Nepali Congress said the government should act on the commission's recommendations "free from political pressure", called for victim compensation, and described the earlier Karki commission report as "incomplete, inadequate and limited in scope".
document_url: {"url": "https://en.himalpress.com/nc-seeks-govts-official-position-on-nhrc-report/", "label": "Source page"}

title: Nepali Congress asks government to state position on NHRC report
description: Congress said the government should act on the commission's recommendations and proceed with legal action, free from political pressure. The article gives no government response.

title: Gurung reappointed home minister; Pun appointed minister
description: Sudan Gurung returned as home minister less than two months after resigning; independent lawmaker Mahabir Pun took the oath as minister for science, technology and innovation. The oath was scheduled for 3 PM at Sheetal Niwas.

title: Probe committee clears Gurung
description: A committee investigating Gurung's finances concluded the allegations could not be substantiated; the Kathmandu Post says it did not consider his landholdings unusual or suspicious, and IANS says it found no established link to the businessman. The report date is not given; the date here is the day of the reappointment reports.

title: Cabinet declares 8 September Gen Z Martyrs' Day
description: The government decided to observe 8 September as Gen Z Martyrs' Day and a public holiday. The 3 September date comes from search-result summaries of other outlets; the Hamro Patro article confirms the decision but not the date.

title: Prime Minister Shah addresses the UN General Assembly
description: Prime Minister Balendra Shah told the 81st UN General Assembly "Our youth have demanded a politics of integrity and accountability". The retrieved speech text does not name the September 2025 protests or the killings.
document_url: {"url": "https://mofa.gov.np/content/1890/address-by-the-rt--hon--prime-minister/", "label": "Source page"}

title: Regmi committee reports on criminal cases against protesters
description: A committee headed by Baburam Regmi reviewed 445 cases naming 1,778 people and advised that charges can be withdrawn only for about 300, because murder, arson and looting cannot be dropped under existing law; 53 cases were already decided by courts. It reported to Home Minister Sudan Gurung on 1 October 2026.

title: Disaster council recommends Rs559.17 billion for flood reconstruction
description: The National Council for Disaster Risk Reduction and Management, chaired by the prime minister, decided to recommend a Rs559.17 billion budget to the finance ministry for 504 plans and programmes. The date is the article date.
